subject: The claims nobody at Veterans Affairs will sign

locus.descriptor: a rented floor across the river where the unsigned files are stacked by year

context.standing: The department has been slower every quarter of this administration. Nothing collapsed and no one resigned; the approvals simply stopped moving, because the only mistake an adjudicator has ever been disciplined for is approving a claim that later looked wrong.
context.precedent: The last government to face this ordered a clearance under a lowered standard, cleared the whole stack in a year, and spent the following four years answering for the fraction of it that was fraud. The clearance is still the thing that government is remembered for.

pressures.want: The Secretary of Veterans Affairs wants money and posts, and will not say out loud that the money alone will not make anyone sign.
Members on both sides want the wait down before they have to stand in a hall and explain it to the families who came to ask.
There is a reporter working through the death certificates of people who died with a claim still open.
The contractors who ran the digitization want the extension they were promised before the slowdown was anyone's problem.

context.inaction: The stack grows by roughly the size of a small city every quarter, the oldest files age past the point where the medical evidence in them can be checked at all, and the department starts closing claims for want of a claimant.
context.unknown: Whether the adjudicators would move faster with more of them, or whether the department has simply taught a generation of its own staff that signing is what gets you punished.

opening.text: Two hundred and sixty-eight thousand claims are sitting unsigned and the median wait is now longer than a year. I am not going to tell you my people are lazy. I am going to tell you that in this department approving a claim is the only decision anyone has ever been punished for, and they have all learned it.

Whatever we do here, we do it with money Congress has not appropriated yet. Hiring adjudicators is a permanent claim on the budget. Clearing the stack under a lowered standard is a one-time payment with a tail of recoveries we will be chasing for years.

There is a reporter working through death certificates, matching them against open claim numbers. Nobody in the room has seen the piece. Everyone in the room knows roughly what it will say, and roughly when.

replies.text: Fill every empty adjudicator post and pay for the overtime. I will go to Congress for it and I will say what it is for.
replies.press: President asks Congress for emergency money to clear the veterans claims stack

commitment.remembered: The administration asked Congress for emergency money to seat every empty adjudicator post rather than lower the standard the claims are judged by.

rejoinder.text: The posts are funded and it will be eleven months before a new adjudicator signs anything alone. In the meantime my experienced people are training the new ones instead of clearing files, so the stack goes up before it goes down. You should know that number is coming.

replies.text: Approve everything under the threshold on the evidence already in the file. Audit afterward and recover what was wrong.
replies.press: Veterans claims below the threshold to be approved on the papers already filed

commitment.remembered: The administration cleared the claims stack by approving everything under the threshold on the papers already filed, and put the checking after the payment.

rejoinder.text: The stack is gone in five months and the department's own auditors put the wrong-payment share somewhere between a twentieth and a twelfth. My lawyers want you to hear the other half now: every recovery is a letter to a veteran saying we want the money back, and there will be tens of thousands of them.

replies.text: The standard stays. Publish the wait, publish the stack, and tell the country why we are not buying the number down.

commitment.remembered: The administration refused to lower the claims standard or to buy the wait down, and published the stack and the wait every month instead.

rejoinder.text: The first monthly publication runs in every paper in the country and the number is worse than anyone outside the department had guessed. Two members who had defended the department all year read it and stopped.

subject: The auditor's report you already tried to stop

locus.descriptor: a windowless reading room where the draft is signed for and signed back

context.standing: The inspector general opened on the department's own numbers, this administration filed notice to remove them, and the notice made the audit public and permanent. The draft has now been finished by the office the removal notice was aimed at, and the law gives the government a comment window and nothing else.
context.precedent: Every previous government that answered an auditor by moving on the auditor learned that the removal is what the country remembers and the finding is what the country believes. None of them recovered the argument afterward.

pressures.want: The Secretary whose department is audited wants the comment to contest every adverse finding, on the record, at length.
The government's own lawyers want a narrow comment that concedes the procedural findings and reserves the rest for litigation.
Two reporters already have the removal notice and are waiting for the report to have both halves of the story.
The committee that opened its own file on the removal wants the comment filed publicly, so it can read the government's answer into its hearing.

context.inaction: The window closes with no comment filed, the report publishes with the adverse findings uncontested, and the committee reads the government's silence into the record as an admission on the day the hearing opens.
context.unknown: Whether the second service that would not sign off on the department's original numbers will say so publicly, or let the audit carry it alone.

opening.text: The audit you filed notice against has reported. Nine of eleven findings are adverse, the removal notice is in the annex, and the comment window closes in thirty days. Whatever we file is published beside the report, in full, and read aloud at the hearing.

The other thing you should hear from me rather than from a broadcast. The service that was asked to confirm the department's original numbers never did. It has not contradicted them either. It is waiting to see what we file.

The draft is read in a room where it has to be signed for on the way in and signed back on the way out. Four people in the building have read all three hundred and forty pages, and none of them are in the room now.

replies.text: Concede the procedure, fund the fix in this year's request, contest the two findings we can win, and withdraw the notice.
replies.press: Government concedes audit findings and withdraws its notice against the inspector general

commitment.remembered: The administration conceded the audit's procedural findings, asked for the money to fix them, and withdrew its notice against the inspector general.

rejoinder.text: The withdrawal is filed and the committee has already moved its hearing up a week, because a government that backs down is a better hearing than a government that fights. The Secretary you did not consult found out from the docket.

replies.text: Contest all nine findings, keep the notice standing, and say plainly that this office answered a policy dispute with an audit.
replies.press: Administration contests every adverse finding and keeps its notice against the auditor standing

commitment.remembered: The administration contested every adverse finding of the audit and left its removal notice against the inspector general standing.

rejoinder.text: The comment is filed and the service that was waiting has stopped waiting. It confirmed nothing, which every paper is now printing as the second agency declining to back us, and that is a sentence we will be carrying for a year.

replies.text: Publish our own file the day before theirs. Everything we have, unredacted, and let the country read both.
replies.press: Government publishes its own unredacted file a day ahead of the audit

commitment.remembered: The administration published its own unredacted file on the audited program a day before the report, and let the country read the two side by side.

rejoinder.text: The file goes out at seven in the morning and by noon three names in it belong to career staff who were never accused of anything and are now being asked to comment on doorsteps. The department's union has a lawyer by the evening.

subject: The {{city}} yards and three weeks of money

locus.descriptor: the barge yards along the river through {{city}}, half of them idle since spring

context.standing: The yards through {{city}} live on federal barge and lock orders, the appropriation those orders are written against runs out in three weeks, and nothing has been agreed to replace it. The yards have already stopped ordering steel for anything past the current hulls.
context.precedent: The last time a government let an order book lapse at a river yard, the yard did not reopen when the money came back. The workforce had gone to the pipeline trade and the crane certifications had expired.

pressures.want: The yard operators want an order placed this week, not a promise, because the steel has a lead time and the promise does not.
Members from the river districts want the orders; members who have spent the year on the deficit want to know what is being cut to pay for them.
The trades want the certifications kept current more than they want any one hull, because the certifications are what makes the next job possible.
The Secretary of Transportation wants the lock work, which is the only part of this the department can defend on its own merits.

context.inaction: The appropriation lapses, the yards lay off through the summer, and the crane and welding certifications expire on a schedule nobody can accelerate afterward.
context.unknown: Whether the yards would actually close or simply run thin for a season. The operators say close. The operators have said close before and did not.

opening.text: Three weeks of appropriation left against the barge and lock program, and the yards through {{city}} have already stopped buying steel past the hulls they are on. Two thousand four hundred jobs, and the part that does not come back is the certifications.

I would rather you heard the arithmetic than the appeal. There is no unspent money in this program. Anything you place this week is placed against next year, and next year is the year we said we were bringing the deficit down.
The operators have said the yards would close twice before and twice they did not. The trades have never said it. This year the trades are saying it.

replies.text: Place the lock orders now against next year's money. The locks are defensible on their own and the steel goes on order this week.

commitment.remembered: The administration placed the lock orders against next year's appropriation so the river yards could buy steel before the current money ran out.

rejoinder.text: Steel is on order and the yards are hiring back. The members who spent the year on the deficit have noticed that next year's program is a fifth committed before next year has been argued about, and one of them said so on the record this afternoon.

replies.text: Fund the certifications and the training, not the hulls. Keep the trade alive through the gap and buy the yards back when there is a budget.

commitment.remembered: The administration funded the crane and welding certifications through the funding gap rather than the hulls, keeping the trade current without placing an order.

rejoinder.text: The certifications hold and about a third of the workforce takes the pipeline work anyway, because a current certification does not pay a mortgage through a summer. The yards will have the papers and not the people.

replies.text: Let it lapse. I am not committing next year's money in a week where nobody has agreed what next year is.

commitment.remembered: The administration let the barge and lock appropriation lapse rather than commit next year's money before next year had been agreed.

rejoinder.text: The layoffs went out on the Friday. The thing I did not put in the briefing, because I did not know it: two of the three yards have already sold crane time to the pipeline contractors through the fall, which means they are not idle waiting for us. They are gone.

premise.reason: The appropriation gate (weeksLeftAtMost 4) establishes the funding clock the week turns on, and a lapsing appropriation is a budget week that deals the same in any phase of the cycle; no cycle reading is presumed.

locus.descriptor: a container terminal where four of our hulls have been at anchor for nine days

transmission.attribution: the counterpart foreign ministry, to our embassy
transmission.text: The berths are assigned by our port authority under our law. When your inspection regime stops treating our exporters as suspects, our schedulers will find your hulls a place. Until then they are welcome to wait, and they are welcome to leave.

context.standing: Four of the country's hulls have been at anchor off the terminal for nine days without a berth assignment. No embargo has been declared and none will be; the scheduling is being done slowly and lawfully, and the counterpart government has said so in writing.
context.precedent: Every government that has answered a slow-walked berth with a seizure has discovered that the shipping insurers reprice the whole route within the week, and that the repricing outlasts the quarrel by years.

pressures.want: The grain shippers want the hulls moving or written off, and they want to know which one this week, because the demurrage is running either way.
The naval staff want authority to escort, and want it before they need it rather than after.
Two governments that use the same terminal want no escort anywhere near it, and have said so twice.
The word blockade is already in print, which is a word that makes half of the answers below unavailable once the country has accepted it.

context.inaction: The hulls sit, the demurrage compounds, the shippers reroute at their own cost and do not come back, and the country loses the route without anything ever having been done to it.
context.unknown: Whether the scheduling is a negotiating position over the inspection regime or the first week of a permanent policy. The counterpart's own port authority may not know either.

opening.text: Nine days at anchor and no berth. Their note says it is scheduling under their own law, and the maddening part is that it is: nothing has been seized, nothing has been declared, and there is no act here for us to answer. There is only a queue that our hulls never reach the front of.

I can put an escort on station in four days. I want you to hear what an escort is before you ask for one. It does not open a berth. It makes every hull in that anchorage a place where somebody could make a mistake, and two of our friends use that terminal.

The word blockade ran in three papers this morning. Nobody in the room used it, and everybody in the room understands that they now have less room than they had yesterday, because a country that has read the word expects an answer sized to it.

replies.text: Offer them the inspection regime. Suspend the exporter checks for a quarter in exchange for the berths, and say so publicly.
replies.press: Exporter checks suspended for a quarter as the anchored hulls are given berths

commitment.remembered: The administration suspended its exporter inspection regime for a quarter in exchange for berthing the anchored hulls, and announced the trade rather than concealing it.

rejoinder.text: All four hulls berthed within a day, which tells you the queue was never a queue. Their trade office has already asked what else the checks might be worth, and that question is now a standing feature of every negotiation we have with them.

replies.text: Put an escort on station and take the hulls in. If berthing is discretionary, our presence in that anchorage is discretionary too.
replies.press: Warships ordered to the anchorage as the government moves to berth its held hulls

commitment.remembered: The administration escorted its anchored hulls into a contested anchorage with warships on station, over the objection of two governments that use the same terminal.

rejoinder.text: The hulls are alongside and nothing was fired. What I did not know when I briefed you: their port authority has moved its own inspection craft into the same water, so we now have two navies and a customs service in one anchorage on standing orders nobody has reconciled.

replies.text: Bring the hulls home and reroute the grain. I will not spend a navy on a berth, and I will say why in the same breath.

commitment.remembered: The administration brought the anchored hulls home and rerouted the grain rather than escort them, writing off the route in public.

rejoinder.text: The hulls turn for home and the insurers reprice the route the same afternoon, which is the part the shippers had been warning about and the part the country will feel. Two of the thirty-one grain contracts are already being renegotiated at the new rate.
